newsitem.title: MEXICO: Dupont says eyeing Mexican petchem plants.
newsitem.headline: Dupont says eyeing Mexican petchem plants.

text.p: U.S. firm DuPont Co said on Friday that it may be interested in a minority stake in one of Mexico's petrochemical plants to be placed on the auction block.
"President (Ernesto Zedillo) reminded us that in fact the industry is opening up so that there would be opportunity for us," DuPont President and CEO John Krol said after a meeting with Zedillo.
"Our approach to that now is going to be to see how the plants that are here will fit in our world wide operations," he told reporters.
Krol added that the company is waiting to see under what scheme the Mexican government decides to sell the plant.
Mexico is privatizing a minority stake in its existing petrochemical complexes, and allowing complete ownership of any new sites. The overdue details on the sale are expected in coming weeks.
DuPont already has several plants operating in Mexico and Krol said any future acquisitions could focus on polymer production.
